title: Brightpath Health — Onboarding Kickoff
description: Kickoff with Brightpath Health covering success goals, privacy requirements, integration plan, and training timeline.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Welcome, everyone, and thanks for joining the Brightpath kickoff. I'm Diego, your customer success manager. With me are Nadia from product, and Kenji, who'll be your integration engineer.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Thanks, Diego. I'm Priyanka Nair, I lead clinical informatics here, and Callum Reeves runs IT integration. We're excited, honestly. We've struggled to understand our patient portal for a long time.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Hi all. I'm the one who'll be asking the annoying security questions, so apologies in advance.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Annoying security questions are welcome. Priyanka, what does success look like in six months?

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Today 41 percent of patients who start booking an appointment in the portal abandon it. I want that under 30 percent by the end of Q1.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: The second goal is knowing which of our nine clinics has the worst drop-off, so we can focus the front-desk teams there.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Good, measurable goals. We'll build the dashboards around exactly that funnel.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Also, the contract covers 85 seats, but I'd like to start with 25 for the pilot.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Let me jump to privacy, since it gates everything. We cannot send protected health information into any analytics tool. No names, no record numbers, no dates of birth.

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: Understood. Our SDK has a property allowlist, so only fields you explicitly name are sent. For patient identity, we recommend a salted hash generated on your side, so we never see the raw ID.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: A salted hash with a key we rotate works. What about free-text fields, like the search box in the portal?

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: I'd exclude those entirely, because people type symptoms into search boxes. I'll send you a list of recommended SDK exclusions, including form text and URL query strings.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Please do. And the data processing addendum, legal countersigned that last week, right?

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Yes, on the 30th. I'll resend you the fully executed copy so you have it on file.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Next, data residency. We need US-only storage.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Your workspace is provisioned in our US-East region, and our CTO, Tobias, can confirm that in writing if your auditors ask.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: One more thing. We heard Lumora had an ingestion outage last week. How stale did the data get, and what stops it from happening again?

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Fair question, and I'd rather address it directly. On October 1st we had about two and a half hours of delayed ingestion. No data was lost. The cause was one large tenant flooding a partition.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: The fix is per-tenant rate limits shipping to production by October 14th, ahead of the Insights 2.0 launch on the 21st.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Okay. I'd like a written summary, with the rate limit numbers.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: I'll send you the incident summary by Friday, including the numbers.

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: For integration, the plan is the JavaScript SDK on the patient portal, plus a server-side connection for the scheduling system's booking-confirmed event.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Our scheduling vendor can send webhooks, but they're sometimes late. Is there a batch option too?

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: Yes, batches of up to 5,000 events per request. I'd use webhooks for freshness and a nightly batch to reconcile.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Fine. We're on a change freeze through October 9th, so I can't touch the portal until the week of the 12th.

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: That works. If I get a staging environment by the 12th, I can have the SDK instrumented and verified with you by the 16th.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: I'll set up the staging access and send you credentials by Monday the 12th.

transcript.speaker: kenji
transcript.text: Event naming matters too. We suggest a verb-object convention like appointment_booked, so the funnels read cleanly.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Our analysts will love that. The scheduling vendor's field names are a mess.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: SSO is the other piece. We use Okta, and we want SCIM provisioning so offboarded staff lose access automatically.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: SSO with SCIM is supported on your plan. Kenji will include the setup guide, and Diego can schedule a call with your Okta admin.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Let's talk about what my team sees. Day one, I want the booking funnel by clinic: portal visit, login, choose provider, choose time, confirm.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: That's one of our standard funnel templates. With Insights 2.0 you'd also get anomaly alerts, so if a clinic's confirm step suddenly drops, you're notified.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: That would have saved us in August, when a scheduling bug cost us a week of bookings and nobody noticed.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Can analysts share dashboards with clinic managers without giving them edit rights?

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Yes, there are viewer roles, and you can schedule a weekly digest per clinic so managers don't have to log in at all.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Managers would love that. They hate new logins.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Exactly the use case. Insights 2.0 launches October 21st, and I'll add Brightpath to the early-access list this week so you get alerts before general availability.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: For training, I suggest two sessions, one for analysts and one for clinic managers. How about October 28th for the analysts?

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: The 28th works. Clinic managers are busier, so can we do them after the first week of November?

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Then November 5th. I'll send calendar holds for both.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: And I'll send the list of the 25 pilot users with their roles by next Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: Let me recap. Callum sends staging access by Monday the 12th. Kenji sends the SDK guide and exclusions list. I send the incident summary and the executed addendum.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Let's schedule a check-in for next Tuesday, October 13th, to review staging progress.

transcript.speaker: diego
transcript.text: One last thing, we also keep a shared channel with each customer. Who should be in it?

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Me, Callum, and two of my analysts. Give me a day to confirm who.

transcript.speaker: priyanka
transcript.text: Works for me. Thank you all, this was clearer than any vendor kickoff we've had.

transcript.speaker: callum
transcript.text: Agreed. Talk next week.

summary.overview: Lumora kicked off onboarding with Brightpath Health, a nine-clinic healthcare network. Their success goal is cutting patient-portal booking abandonment from 41% to under 30% by the end of Q1, starting with a 25-user pilot. Privacy was the main gating topic: no PHI will be sent, identities will be hashed client-side, and free-text fields will be excluded. The team agreed on staging access by October 12th, SDK verification by the 16th, trainings on October 28th and November 5th, and a written incident summary after Callum asked about the October 1st outage.

Goal is to reduce portal booking abandonment from 41% to under 30% by end of Q1 and find the worst clinics out of nine.
Contract covers 85 seats; the pilot starts with 25.

notes.title: Data privacy and security
bullets: No protected health information may be sent; the SDK allowlist and a client-side salted hash for patient IDs will be used.
Free-text fields, form text and URL query strings will be excluded.
Data processing addendum was countersigned on September 30th; workspace is in US-East.
Callum asked about the October 1st outage; Diego owes a written summary with rate limit numbers by Friday.

notes.title: Technical integration plan
bullets: Plan is the JavaScript SDK on the portal plus server-side booking-confirmed events via webhooks, with a nightly batch reconcile.
Brightpath is in a change freeze through October 9th; staging access arrives by Monday the 12th and SDK verification by the 16th.
Okta SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported on their plan.

notes.title: Dashboards, training, and timeline
bullets: Day-one dashboard is the booking funnel by clinic: visit, login, choose provider, choose time, confirm.
Insights 2.0 anomaly alerts would catch issues like August's scheduling bug; Brightpath goes on the early-access list.
Training on October 28th for analysts and November 5th for clinic managers; pilot user list due next Wednesday.

notes.title: Recap and follow-up
bullets: Recap of owners: Callum on staging, Kenji on SDK guide, Diego on incident summary and addendum.
